minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee reviewed the FY24 request list without a vote, split over whether funding sources are in its scope.
minutes.summary: The committee went through updated town manager and school department information on the capital request list and discussed cemetery, Flat Hill drainage, building and vehicle items. A member pressed for the town manager's intent on using the special purpose stabilization fund for the ambulance, and the chair held that funding is outside the committee's scope. Members will bring ranking sheets to the next Monday meeting; no substantive votes were taken.

Estimated below the capital threshold, so the town manager recommended removing it from capital and covering it in the operating budget.
Multi-year staged turf work at the North and South cemeteries.
Estimate rose when five days of work were added; a lower option was discussed and members suggested spreading the work over years.
Engineering is a small share of the request and design is funded from FY23 capital funds; members questioned spending on private-property drainage without a plan.
Recaulking will be paid from the school maintenance budget, not capital; full window replacement would cost far more.
Project is listed in the plan; a member recalled a much larger abatement number years ago.
Fund said to hold a large balance for ambulances and fire trucks; using it for the capital plan would raise the vote threshold.
Traditional sources are expected to fall short of the request list; past requests ran higher.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee went through the FY24 capital request list and took no votes.
Members split on whether the town manager's plan to fund an ambulance from the special purpose stabilization fund is within the committee's scope; the chair held it is not.
The town manager's updated cemetery requests were reviewed; the hedge work was recommended for the operating budget instead of capital.
Members questioned Flat Hill Road drainage on private property, the Senior Center lot estimate, and school security items including the contested safety film.
Members will bring completed ranking sheets to the Monday meeting; the Wednesday the 14th was set as the last meeting before the list goes to the town manager.

why_it_matters: The ranked list this committee sends to the town manager shapes which capital projects reach town meeting, where residents vote on borrowing and on drawing from stabilization funds.
Traditional capital sources were described as falling short of the request list, so some items may rely on other funding, such as the stabilization fund, which carries a higher vote threshold.
